- PII redaction pipeline (pseudonymization) can run before any persistent metrics are stored; we can scope the fields we scrub.
- Aggregated usage metrics (token counts, error rates) are retained for billing and platform health; we can supply limited exports for your accounting team.

Hi Alice — looping in technical details from the engineering side. Short answers first: 24-hour retention is feasible for hosted endpoints as a configured policy; for Dedicated/Private we can configure immediate drop. PII redaction can be applied inline but with caveats. Details below.

Technical details / constraints:
- Retention layers: request/response payloads (raw) -> ephemeral KV cache -> short-term logs (configurable TTL) -> aggregated metrics (billing). We can set TTLs per-environment.
- 0-retention on raw payloads: on Dedicated/Private we can route telemetry to a null sink immediately. On hosted we can approximate 0-retention by dropping raw logs at ingress, but a tiny operational buffer (seconds) exists for routing; we can guarantee deletion within 10s of ingestion for requests if that meets your definition.
- PII redaction: we offer an inline pseudonymization transform. By default it uses reversible tokens for debugging; we can switch to irreversible hashing (SHA-256 + salt) for your account. Let us know which fields you require redacted.
- Billing & audit: aggregated token counts and per-route metrics are stored for 13 months by default for billing and trend analysis; we can provide an export for invoicing and reduce the storage window for FinCorp to 90 days if required.

Attached: data-retention-options.xlsx (spreadsheet showing options: immediate-drop, 24h, 7d, aggregated-only; tradeoffs and monitoring impact).

Recommended next steps: 
- Rafael/Legal to draft a DPA addendum with: explicit deletion SLA, proof of deletion process, and irreversibility clause for PII.
- Engineering call to confirm field-level redaction list and salt rotation policy.

I can join the call on 2026-10-15 10:00 PT. Rafael / Marissa — please confirm and I’ll prepare a short tech slide.

Thanks,
Camila
